reasoning: The statement joins two different activities: writing up the classroom rules and procedures, usually in a syllabus or a posted set at the start of a term, and enforcing them live day to day. Y separates the written rule set, which administrators can review, from the interpersonal enforcement, as step 1 asks.

Objectives are written per lesson or unit and shared with students by posting them or putting them in materials, so communicating them is the delivery of the same written item. Any spoken explanation in class is already instruction under 6640. X's single DISCRETE item is better.

Teachers adapt methods and materials mainly while planning a lesson or unit, and that produces adapted plans and materials. Delivering the adapted lesson live is already covered by 6640. Y's single DISCRETE part avoids splitting one planning deliverable into a live part that duplicates instruction.

Program development work by teachers combines committee discussion with written outputs such as program proposals, evaluations and curriculum revisions that administrators review. X captures both. Y codes everything as INTERPERSONAL and loses the documents that are checked.

The real split is between desk work (selecting and ordering) and hands-on work (storing, issuing, counting). For a classroom teacher the inventory 'record' is usually just the result of the count. Y's third part is thin, so X's two-part split is enough.

Sponsoring a club or contest involves both organizing work with an output (schedules, registrations, trip and event arrangements that staff and students rely on) and live supervision of students. X splits these as the instructions ask, while Y codes everything as interpersonal.

Hall, cafeteria and bus duty is live supervision of students, which is INTERPERSONAL, not PHYSICAL hands-on work. Library desk help is service to a student who is waiting. X's types fit the definitions better than Y's single PHYSICAL part.

Configuring supportive software or devices is screen-based work with a usable output, while setting up devices and helping students reach facilities is hands-on. The physical-versus-computer rule requires a split, so Y is correct.
